scripts.check: npm run tokens:check && npm run honesty:check && npm run camera:check && npm run fonts:check && npm run api:types:check && npm run guards && npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm run format:check && npm run test && npm run test:e2e

comment:overrides: image-size — GHSA-w3rx-r6r6-pgpr, an infinite loop in the ICNS parser. It
texture-compressor is a Node CLI for KTX/basis compression that no browser
bundle on any of our surfaces calls. The honest fix is still to remove the
vulnerable code rather than to argue it is unreachable, because 'unreachable
today' is a claim about the current call graph and not about the next one.
2.x rather than 2.0.3: the advisory's ceiling is 2.0.2, and pinning to the
first patched patch release would leave this entry to be rediscovered by the
next advisory in the same file. The major is safe here because the only
consumer invokes it through its CLI, and `npm run build` plus the clay and
golden suites are what proves that rather than this paragraph.
The alternative npm offers is `audit fix --force`, which 'fixes' this by
DOWNGRADING deck.gl from 9.4.1 to 9.1.0 — a major step backwards past the
version §E20's 2D tier is written against. Declined.
